title: Pricing a dish from its food cost
lede: The menu price has to cover the cost of the ingredients several times over. Move the sliders and watch what happens to the price.
intent: Learners can calculate a menu price from a portion cost and a target food cost percentage, and explain how a change in cost affects price.
goal: calculate a menu price from a portion cost and a target food cost percentage.

outputs.label: Menu price before GST
outputs.explain: Portion cost divided by the target food cost percentage.

outputs.label: Price the customer pays
outputs.explain: The menu price with 10 per cent GST added.

outputs.label: Gross profit per plate
outputs.explain: What is left of the price before GST once the ingredients are paid for.

challenges.prompt: Your supplier puts the portion cost up to $11. Keep food cost at 30 per cent. What does the menu price before GST need to be?
challenges.hint: Set the portion cost to $11 and the target back to 30 per cent.
challenges.success: About $36.67. A $2 rise in cost needs a price rise of about $6.67 to hold the same percentage, because the price has to cover the cost more than three times over.

challenges.prompt: A competitor sells the same dish for $32 before GST. At a portion cost of $11, roughly what food cost percentage would you be running if you matched them?
challenges.hint: Leave the cost at $11 and move the target until the price is close to $32.
challenges.success: About 34 per cent. Matching the competitor's price costs you around four points of margin on every plate.

challenges.prompt: Find a portion cost and a target that give a price before GST of exactly $40. What does the customer pay?
challenges.hint: Try $12 at 30 per cent, or $10 at 25 per cent.
challenges.success: $44. GST goes on top of the price you set, so work the price out first and then add 10 per cent.

teach.watchFor: Learners adding the target percentage to the cost (a markup) instead of dividing by it. Ask them to check: at a 30 per cent food cost, is the cost 30 per cent of the price?

sources.label: Food cost percentage, standard hospitality costing: cost divided by sale price excluding GST
sources.note: Check the convention and the GST treatment against your unit's costing guide.
